trueExplanation: The glass is so clean because the curator spent three hours polishing it right before the theft.
heistExplanation: The thief opened the case so cleanly that the dust pattern on the glass is the only thing that moved.

reconstructionUses.heistExplanation: The display case was opened without forcing the lock, allowing the artifact to disappear before any alarm noticed the difference.
A near-perfect replica went into the case before anyone looked closely, so the museum admired the fake for hours.

trueExplanation: The technician left a sticky note inside saying "DO NOT TOUCH – I'LL FIX IT TOMORROW".
heistExplanation: The thief read the note as "VIP access" and slipped a bypass in while the system was already half-asleep.

reconstructionUses.heistExplanation: The thief exploited the panel's unfinished repair and bypassed the security circuit before it could report the intrusion.
A temporary bridge across the exposed wiring silenced the alarm without cutting power to the whole museum.

trueExplanation: The card is snapped right through the word "EXPIRED" on the back.
heistExplanation: The thief had a functioning card; this one died bravely in a failed attempt at overtime access.

reconstructionUses.heistExplanation: The thief cloned the badge credentials, using the original only long enough to copy its access data.
A copied access credential convinced the door system that an authorised staff member was entering.
The thief triggered a routine staff-door event at exactly the right moment, manipulating the control room into focusing on a harmless access alert while the real route remained unwatched.

trueExplanation: There is a price tag the size of a postcard still dangling from the brim.
heistExplanation: The thief chose a more subtle disguise; it is hard to blend in when your hat has its own orbit.

reconstructionUses.heistExplanation: The thief used an extravagant visitor outfit to become memorable for the wrong reasons while their face stayed hidden in plain sight.
The hat created exactly the kind of minor scene that makes a bored guard look up, walk over, and stop watching the gallery.

item: Crime board with photos and strings
trueExplanation: The red string connects suspects to a big circle labeled "MAYBE?".
heistExplanation: The thief made sure their own photo never left a trace, not even a blurry corner on this board.

reconstructionUses.heistExplanation: The thief mapped exhibition schedules, staff routines, and insurance values until one artifact stood out as the perfect target.
The connected photos and schedules revealed a route through the museum with fewer witnesses and slower response times.
The board linked a minor incident to the exact wing where a distraction would draw security away from the target.

trueExplanation: The casing is stamped "training only" and smells more of blanks than danger.
heistExplanation: The thief planned it so well that nobody had time—or need—to fire anything real.

reconstructionUses.heistExplanation: A blank round caused a loud but harmless panic, pulling guards toward the wrong end of the museum.
The thief fired a warning shot into the air, creating just enough fear to clear the route without a direct confrontation.
The casing was planted to make the theft look like a violent break-in, drawing the investigation toward the wrong kind of suspect.

trueExplanation: A sign nearby says "Staff only – do not swing", which someone obviously ignored.
heistExplanation: The thief chose stairs over circus tricks; stealth looks less impressive but works every time.

reconstructionUses.heistExplanation: The thief descended through an upper service opening, avoiding every public entrance and staffed door.
The rope gave the thief a route to a high gallery ledge that could not be reached from the public floor.
Once the artifact was secured, the rope offered a fast exit over the same upper route before the building locked down.

trueExplanation: The status screen proudly says "UPTIME: 999 DAYS" – which no real system would brag about.
heistExplanation: The thief did not even touch the panel; why fight a system that is clearly already living in fantasy.

reconstructionUses.heistExplanation: The thief exploited the system's neglected maintenance mode to pass a false all-clear to the alarm network.
A carefully timed command stopped the alarm from escalating while leaving the normal status lights reassuringly green.
The thief redirected one camera to a harmless maintenance feed, leaving the target gallery temporarily unseen.
